title: Genetic and Epigenetic Fidelity, Passage History and QA

content.overview: Clonal propagation aims to preserve identity, but long-term in-vitro culture should not be treated as biologically frozen. Passage history, regeneration route, stress and culture conditions can influence phenotype and epigenetic state, so high-value germplasm needs a fidelity strategy.

vocabulary.definition: Genetic or phenotypic variation arising among plants regenerated through tissue culture.
A heritable or persistent change in gene regulation that does not require a change in DNA sequence.
One transfer or subculture generation in an in-vitro propagation system.

sections.title: Different regeneration routes carry different fidelity questions
sections.body: Propagation through organized meristems is generally managed differently from callus-associated regeneration because de-novo regeneration can introduce additional variation risk and requires stronger identity controls.

sections.title: Recent cannabis work detected culture-associated epigenetic change
sections.body: A 2025 multi-genotype study reported progressive DNA hypomethylation during in-vitro culture, showing why long-term culture history should be recorded even when plants appear phenotypically normal.

sections.title: QA should combine identity, history and phenotype
sections.body: No single test proves complete fidelity. Source identity, passage count, morphology, performance and—where justified—molecular or cytometric tests provide complementary evidence.

workedExamples: A mother line with many passages but normal appearance may still warrant periodic comparison with a low-passage reference line.
A regenerated plant with abnormal morphology should be quarantined from breeder stock even before a molecular cause is known.
commonMistakes: Assuming clonal means permanently identical under every culture route.
Using appearance alone as proof of genetic fidelity.
content.practicalApplication: Define a germplasm QA plan with source ID, passage ceiling or review interval, retained reference material, phenotype checks and escalation criteria for molecular testing.
content.summary: Tissue culture is powerful for germplasm multiplication and preservation, but fidelity is an actively managed quality attribute. Passage history and verification belong in the propagation record.
